title: Kúnigseq Visits the Land of Shades
subtitle: A visitor must not eat the underworld berries

learningObjectives.text: What warning does Kúnigseq's helping spirit give about the berries?
What does Kúnigseq say after seeing his dead family?

visit.author: Greenlandic storytellers, collected by Knud Rasmussen
visit.excerpt: There was once a wizard whose name was Kúnigseq. One day, when he was about to call on his helping spirits and make a flight down into the underworld, he gave orders that the floor should be swilled with salt water, to take off the evil smell which might otherwise frighten his helping spirits away. Then he began to call upon his helping spirits, and without moving his body, began to pass downward through the floor. And down he went. On his way he came to a reef, which was covered with weed, and therefore so slippery that none could pass that way. And as he could not pass, his helping spirit lay down beside him, and by placing his foot upon the spirit, he was able to pass. And on he went, and came to a great slope covered with heather. Far down in the underworld, men say, the land is level, and the hills are small; there is sun down there, and the sky is also like that which we see from the earth. Suddenly he heard one crying: "Here comes Kúnigseq." By the side of a little river he saw some children looking for greyfish. And before he had reached the houses of men, he met his mother, who had gone out to gather berries. When he came up to her, she tried again and again to kiss him, but his helping spirit thrust her aside. "He is only here on a visit," said the spirit. Then she offered him some berries, and these he was about to put in his mouth, when the spirit said: "If you eat of them, you will never return.
visit.note: Verbatim English rendering by Worster from stories collected by Rasmussen in Greenland. The book title uses an outdated ethnonym; this lesson identifies the collection's Greenland scope.

narrativeBlocks.title: A journey below the floor
narrativeBlocks.body: Kúnigseq calls his helping spirits and travels down into the underworld, where he meets his dead mother.

narrativeBlocks.title: A warning at the boundary

narrativeBlocks.title: A visit has rules
narrativeBlocks.body: His spirit companion says that if Kúnigseq eats the berries, he will never return. The dead mother invites him to stay, but he says he will come back when he dies.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not infer one uniform afterlife
narrativeBlocks.body: This is one Greenland story in Rasmussen's collection, translated and edited by Worster. The title's historical spelling and the story's details belong to this edition and its source context.

narrativeBlocks.title: A visit differs from a permanent journey
narrativeBlocks.body: The warning about eating marks a boundary between the living visitor and the dead community in this particular tale.

quiz.prompt: What warning does Kúnigseq's helping spirit give about the berries?

choices.text: They will turn him into a raven
If he eats them, he will never return
They will make the Sun move faster

quiz.explanation: The spirit warns that eating the berries will prevent Kúnigseq from returning.
